caesar_grunt.notes: Part of the Florida/SE grunt complex. Verify current state rules.

tomtate_grunt.notes: Part of the Florida/SE grunt complex. Verify current state rules.

porcupinefish.notes: CAUTION: Porcupinefish contain tetrodotoxin — do not eat. Handle carefully and release quickly.

orangespotted_filefish.notes: No specific regulations for orangespotted filefish. Release recommended.

smooth_trunkfish.notes: Smooth trunkfish secrete pahutoxin when stressed — do not mix with other fish in a livewell. Release recommended.

scrawled_filefish.notes: No specific regulations for scrawled filefish. Edible once rough skin removed — most are released.

great_hammerhead.notes: Great hammerhead sharks are PROHIBITED in the Atlantic and Gulf under federal HMS regulations. Release immediately. Critically Endangered — minimize handling, use dehooking tools in the water.

bonnethead_shark.notes: Bonnethead sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Requires federal HMS Angling Permit from a vessel. 1-fish vessel limit. Mostly released.

inshore_shark.notes: Inshore shark fishing requires a federal HMS Angling Permit. Most small coastal sharks have a 1-fish vessel daily limit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

nurse_shark_juvenile.notes: Same regulations as adult nurse shark. Release recommended.

atlantic_sharpnose_shark_juvenile.notes: Same HMS regulations as adult sharpnose shark. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

spanish_mackerel_atlantic.notes: Spanish mackerel: 14-inch FL minimum on Atlantic coast, 12-inch Gulf. 15-fish daily bag limit in most states. Verify current ASMFC and GMFMC rules.

king_mackerel_small.notes: King mackerel have a 24-inch minimum and 3-fish bag limit in most states. Gulf regulations may differ. Verify current SAFMC, GMFMC and state rules.

little_tunny_small.notes: No specific bag limit for little tunny (false albacore). Same as adult little tunny. Not recommended for eating by most anglers.

bonito_atlantic.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic bonito. Verify current state rules.

florida_pompano_juvenile.min_size: 11 in (FL) — must be released if under minimum
florida_pompano_juvenile.bag_limit: 6 per day when at or above minimum size
florida_pompano_juvenile.notes: Juvenile pompano under the minimum size must be released. Same regulations as adult Florida pompano.

permit_small.min_size: 22 in fork length (same as flats permit)
permit_small.bag_limit: 2 per person per day (same as flats permit)
permit_small.notes: Same regulations as permit (flats). Verify current state rules.

permit_large.notes: Same permit regulations apply at any size. Verify current FL FWC and state rules.

menhaden_atlantic.notes: Not caught on hook and line. Used as bait and chum. Commercial harvest managed by ASMFC.

gizzard_shad_tidal.notes: Cast net only — not caught on hook and line. Typically used as bait.

cobia_near_pier.notes: Atlantic cobia managed by ASMFC. 1 fish per angler. Very popular spring sight-fishing target.

cobia_offshore.notes: Same size and bag limit as near-pier cobia.

atlantic_croaker_large.notes: Not regulated in most states. Some states have size or possession limits for commercial harvest. Check state rules.

blacktip_shark.notes: NOAA HMS Angling Permit required if targeting sharks. Catch-and-release encouraged. Never cut fins (federal shark finning ban).

atlantic_sharpnose_shark.notes: Small coastal shark — no minimum size. HMS Angling Permit required.

skipjack_tuna_shore.notes: Federal pelagic fish — no HMS permit needed for recreational hook-and-line. Dark flesh — best used as bait.

tilefish_sand.notes: Not managed separately from other tilefish in most SE states. Check state rules.

atlantic_spadefish_pier.notes: Not heavily regulated. Spadefish are excellent table fare — white, mild flesh.

sea_bream_pinfish.notes: Primarily used as live bait. Catch by cast net or tiny hook with shrimp.

grass_porgy.notes: Not separately regulated in most states.

sheepshead_porgy.notes: Not separately regulated — falls under general reef fish or porgy rules.

bull_shark_inshore.notes: HMS permit required. Catch-and-release strongly recommended.

atlantic_sturgeon_catch_and_release.notes: ESA ENDANGERED. Illegal to target, possess, or harm. Release immediately. Report to NOAA: 1-800-853-1964.

goliath_grouper_encounter.notes: Illegal to harvest or possess. FL: cannot be removed from water without scientific permit.

cobia_atlantic.notes: NOAA Atlantic cobia plan. 1 fish per day. Popular spring sight-fishing near VA Beach/Chesapeake Bay mouth.

bluefish_large.notes: ASMFC 3-fish bag limit. Use wire or heavy mono leader — razor teeth.

bluefish_snapper_blues.notes: Same 3-fish bag limit. Wire or heavy mono leader required.

weakfish_sea_trout.notes: ASMFC: 1 fish per day. Critically low population. Handle gently — fragile mouths.

manta_ray_encounter.notes: Cannot be targeted or harassed in US federal waters.

whale_shark_encounter.notes: Illegal to target or harm. Observe from 6 ft minimum distance. Do not ride or touch.

pufferfish_northern.notes: SKIN IS TOXIC — do not eat skin. Properly cleaned northern puffer (sea squab) is edible and considered a delicacy.

atlantic_halfbeak.notes: Primarily used as offshore trolling bait (ballyhoo). No regulations.

cobia_early_season.notes: Same rules as regular cobia. Atlantic and Gulf cobia share 33-inch minimum. 1 fish per day.

southern_flounder_gigging.notes: Gigging regulations same as rod-and-reel limits. TX has restricted fall gigging season at pass mouths.

mako_shark_shortfin.notes: HMS Angling Permit required. Catch-and-release strongly encouraged — depleted population.

pacific_white_shark_encounter.notes: Illegal to target or harm in US waters.

swordfish_daytime_deep_drop.notes: HMS Angling Permit required. Minimum 47-inch lower jaw fork length.

blue_marlin_gulf.notes: HMS Angling Permit required. Catch-and-release strongly encouraged. 99-inch minimum if retaining.

largemouth_bass_tidal.notes: Freshwater license required. State freshwater bass regulations apply in tidal freshwater zones.

atlantic_mackerel_shore.notes: Very perishable — ice immediately. ASMFC managed commercially; no recreational bag limit.

longfin_squid.notes: EGI squid jigs under pier lights at night. Ink stains permanently. Excellent bait and eating.

spot_croaker.notes: 200-fish/day bag limit per angler; no size minimum. Spot are one of the most popular pier species in North Carolina.

summer_flounder.notes: North Carolina state waters: 12-inch minimum, 6/day bag limit. Federal waters have different limits. Verify 2026 state and federal rules with NC DMF.

black_drum.notes: Black drum in North Carolina: 14-inch minimum, 10/day bag limit. Common around inlets and piers. Verify with NC DMF.

atlantic_croaker.notes: Atlantic croaker in North Carolina: no minimum size, 100-fish/day bag limit. One of the most popular surf and pier fish in NC. Verify current rules with NC DMF.

great_hammerhead_shark.notes: Great hammerhead sharks are a prohibited species under NOAA federal shark regulations — they may NOT be harvested or possessed. If caught, they must be released immediately with minimal harm. All anglers fishing for sharks in Atlantic/Gulf federal waters must have a valid NOAA HMS Angling permit. Verify current prohibited species list with NOAA.

crevalle_jack.notes: Crevalle jack in North Carolina: no minimum size or bag limit. Common in warm months. Verify with NC DMF.

red_grouper.season: Open year-round in South Atlantic federal waters
red_grouper.notes: North Carolina red grouper: 20-inch TL minimum, 3/day aggregate grouper (South Atlantic rules). Verify with NC DMF and NOAA/SAFMC.

striped_bass.season: Seasonal — check NJ DEP for open dates
striped_bass.notes: Regulations have changed in recent years and may include slot limits. Verify with NJ DEP. ASMFC measures for 2025-2026 may differ. Verify current slot limits and open seasons with NJ DEP.

summer_flounder.notes: Minimum size may change annually. Verify current year's rules with NJ DEP. Minimum size and bag limit are set annually by NOAA and NJ DEP. Verify 2026 regulations before fishing — limits change each year.

black_sea_bass.season: Seasonal — check NJ DEP for open dates
black_sea_bass.notes: Season and bag limits vary. Verify current rules with NJ DEP. Minimum size and bag limit reviewed annually. Verify 2026 regulations with NJ DEP.

bluefish.notes: Federal bag limit applies. Verify current limits.

tautog.season: Seasonal — check NJ DEP for open dates
tautog.notes: Bag limit varies by season. Verify current rules with NJ DEP.

scup.notes: Verify current limits with NJ DEP.

weakfish.notes: Stock is depleted; bag limit is very restrictive. Verify current rules with NJ DEP.

red_drum.notes: Verify current limits with NJ DEP.

longfin_squid.notes: No size or bag restrictions for recreational anglers.

blue_shark.bag_limit: No specific state limit; HMS federal regulations apply
blue_shark.notes: Consult NOAA Highly Migratory Species regulations. Fins must remain naturally attached.

winter_flounder.notes: Verify current NJ DEP Marine rules; season and bag may change.

atlantic_cod.season: Open year-round; federal closures may apply
atlantic_cod.notes: Verify federal groundfish area closures before offshore fishing.

pollock.notes: Pollock are plentiful in NJ waters in fall and winter.

spanish_mackerel.notes: Summer visitor to NJ; verify current NJ DEP rules.

cobia.notes: Summer visitor to NJ. Verify current NJ DEP limits.

atlantic_bluefin_tuna.min_size: 73 in curved fork length (school/large school); 27 in (Highly Migratory Species)
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.bag_limit: Varies by HMS permit category; General category: 1 per vessel per trip
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.season: General category: June 1 – Nov 14 (approx); varies by NOAA in-season adjustments
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.notes: Bluefin tuna require a federal Highly Migratory Species permit. Size categories and quotas change in-season — ALWAYS verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

atlantic_mackerel.notes: No minimum size. Federal mackerel quota applies to commercial; recreational is generally open.

porbeagle_shark.notes: Prohibited species. Must be immediately released.

mahi_mahi.notes: No closed season; verify any changes to current state or federal rules.

oceanic_whitetip_shark.notes: Oceanic whitetip shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

silky_shark.notes: Silky shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

common_thresher_shark.notes: Common thresher require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify NOAA HMS rules for current season and limits.

atlantic_wolffish.notes: Atlantic wolffish are a species of concern. Retention is prohibited in US federal waters. Release immediately.

atlantic_bonito.notes: No state regulations for Atlantic bonito in most states.

atlantic_blue_marlin.notes: Atlantic blue marlin require an HMS recreational permit. 99 in LJFL minimum. Strong conservation ethic — most released. Verify NOAA HMS rules.

little_tunny.notes: No size or bag limit for little tunny in most states. Primarily catch-and-release fishery; flesh is strong-flavored.

bay_anchovy.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

mummichog.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

striped_killifish.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

walleye_coastal.notes: Walleye in tidal waters follow state freshwater regulations; verify local rules as tidal sections may have different limits than inland waters.

chain_pickerel.notes: Chain pickerel in tidal freshwater zones follow state freshwater regulations. Verify current tidal vs. non-tidal rules.

swordfish.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules and possession limits. Strong conservation ethic — most are released.

bigeye_tuna.season: Open year-round; Atlantic bigeye quota applies
bigeye_tuna.notes: Bigeye tuna are under ICCAT quota management. Verify current NOAA HMS possession limits. Charter captains must check current quota availability.

atlantic_menhaden.notes: No recreational bag or size limit for menhaden in most Atlantic states. Commercial harvest is managed by ASMFC. Cast-netting for live bait is widely practiced.

cownose_ray.notes: No state regulations for cownose ray in most Mid-Atlantic states. Some states run bow-fishing and bowfishing tournaments during spring/fall runs.

barndoor_skate.min_size: None (prohibited to retain in federal waters)
barndoor_skate.bag_limit: 0 in federal waters; verify state rules
barndoor_skate.notes: Barndoor skates are a species of concern and retention is prohibited in US federal waters. Release immediately.

silver_hake_whiting.notes: No federal or state recreational bag or size limit for silver hake/whiting. Commercial quota applies under NEFMC. A common winter nearshore species.

offshore_hake.notes: No specific recreational regulations for offshore hake. Verify current NEFMC rules for any updated stock-specific guidance.

atlantic_spanish_mackerel.bag_limit: 15 per person per day in most states
atlantic_spanish_mackerel.notes: Spanish mackerel regulations are similar across SE/Mid-Atlantic states. FL has a 12-inch minimum. Verify current state rules.

atlantic_pollock.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
atlantic_pollock.notes: No recreational bag limit for pollock in most New England states. Excellent eating — check for any current NEFMC updates.

witch_flounder.notes: Witch flounder (gray sole) — excellent eating. No specific recreational size/bag limit in most states.

american_plaice.notes: American plaice (dab) — no specific recreational limit in most states.

greenland_halibut.notes: Greenland halibut (turbot) — primarily commercial species; no specific recreational regulations in US waters.

gulf_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
gulf_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

northern_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

southern_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
southern_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

wahoo_atlantic.bag_limit: 2 per person per day in most states
wahoo_atlantic.notes: Wahoo regulations vary by state. Most SE/Gulf states have a 2-fish bag limit. Verify current state rules.

black_sea_bass_atlantic.min_size: 12.5-13 in TL (varies by state and season)
black_sea_bass_atlantic.season: Check current NOAA/state season calendar — varies annually
black_sea_bass_atlantic.notes: Black sea bass regulations are complex and change annually. Verify current state and federal rules before fishing.

spot_atlantic.notes: No size or bag limit for Atlantic spot in most states. A beloved fall panfish throughout the Mid-Atlantic.

tilefish_golden.notes: Golden tilefish have a 7-fish bag limit in most Mid-Atlantic and NE states under MAFMC rules. Verify current state and federal rules.

atlantic_blacktip_shark.notes: Shark regulations require a federal HMS Angling Permit for non-Atlantic coastal state recreational fishing. Verify current NOAA HMS rules for blacktip shark.

spinner_shark.notes: Spinner sharks are managed under NOAA HMS shark rules. Verify current regulations.

caribbean_reef_shark.notes: Managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current federal shark regulations. Practice catch-and-release.

lemon_shark.notes: Lemon sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current regulations.

sand_tiger_shark.season: Check current state and federal rules
sand_tiger_shark.notes: Sand tiger sharks are protected in some states (NC, VA). Release immediately. Check current NOAA HMS and state rules.

skipjack_tuna_atlantic.notes: No specific recreational bag limit for skipjack tuna in most Atlantic states. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

northern_puffer.notes: No specific regulations for northern puffer. Properly cleaning pufferfish is important — the liver, skin, and gonads contain tetrodotoxin. Only eat the skinned back-strap meat.

spotted_eagle_ray.notes: Spotted eagle rays have a venomous tail barb — handle with extreme caution. They are a protected species in some states. Minimize handling and release quickly.

dover_sole.notes: Part of the flatfish aggregate limit. Verify current state rules.

rex_sole.notes: Included in flatfish aggregate. Verify state rules.

surfperch_aggregate.min_size: Varies by species; most have no minimum size
surfperch_aggregate.notes: Surfperch (pile perch, rainbow seaperch, striped seaperch, pink seaperch, shiner perch, etc.) fall under a 20-fish daily bag aggregate in most Pacific states. Verify current state rules.

chilipepper_rockfish.season: Open most of year; check depth restrictions
chilipepper_rockfish.notes: Part of the rockfish complex. Verify current area/depth rules.

shortbelly_rockfish.notes: No specific limit; part of rockfish aggregate.

greenstriped_rockfish.notes: Part of rockfish aggregate. Verify current rules.

pacific_sand_dab.notes: Pacific sand dabs have no bag or size limit in most Pacific states. They are among the most lightly regulated flatfish species.

speckled_sand_dab.notes: No specific regulations; verify current state rules.

butter_sole.bag_limit: 10 per day (flatfish aggregate in some areas)
butter_sole.notes: Part of the general flatfish group. Verify current state flatfish aggregate rules.

sand_sole.bag_limit: 10 per day (flatfish aggregate in some areas)
sand_sole.notes: Part of the general flatfish group. Verify current state flatfish aggregate rules.

white_croaker.notes: No size limit for white croaker. Check local consumption advisories — some Southern California harbors have fish consumption warnings due to sediment contamination.

pacific_mackerel.notes: No state size or bag limit for Pacific mackerel. Abundance varies with ocean conditions.

jack_mackerel_pacific.notes: No specific regulations for Pacific jack mackerel in most states.

surf_smelt.bag_limit: 10 lbs per person (or check current dip-net rules)
surf_smelt.season: Open during run seasons (varies by beach)
surf_smelt.notes: Surf smelt dip-netting rules vary by location and run. Check ODFW or WDFW for current beach-specific regulations before dip-netting.

night_smelt.notes: Night smelt dip-netting permitted at designated beaches. Verify ODFW/WDFW current rules.

leopard_shark.notes: Leopard sharks are managed under California Leopard/Soupfin/Smoothhound complex. Verify current CDFW rules. Most anglers practice catch and release.

soupfin_shark.notes: Soupfin shark has no specific size limit but counts toward the general elasmobranch bag limit. Verify current CDFW/ODFW/WDFW rules.

gray_smoothhound.notes: Gray and brown smoothhounds share the general Pacific shark bag limit. No specific size limit. Verify current state rules.

brown_smoothhound.notes: Gray and brown smoothhounds share the general Pacific shark bag limit. No specific size limit. Verify current state rules.

pacific_electric_ray.notes: No specific regulations for Pacific electric ray. WARNING: they deliver a strong electric shock — never handle directly. Cut the leader to release.

pacific_tomcod.notes: No specific bag or size limit for Pacific tomcod in most Pacific states. Verify current state rules.

eulachon.bag_limit: 10 lbs per day during open seasons
eulachon.season: Open during designated river run periods (typically Feb-April)
eulachon.notes: Eulachon harvest is heavily regulated by river and by year based on run strength. Some rivers are closed in poor-run years. Always check ODFW before dip-netting.

white_seaperch.notes: White seaperch count toward the general surfperch aggregate bag limit. Verify current state rules.

pacific_whiting.notes: No specific recreational regulations for Pacific whiting. The commercial fishery is managed under PFMC. Check current CDFW/ODFW/WDFW rules.

blacksmith_pacific.notes: Blacksmith are part of the general nearshore fish regulations in California. Verify current CDFW rules.

plainfin_midshipman.notes: No specific regulations for plainfin midshipman. Mild venom in dorsal spines — handle with care.

cowcod.season: Closed — Cowcod Conservation Areas (CCAs) restrict access
cowcod.notes: Cowcod retention is prohibited in California and in federal Cowcod Conservation Areas. Release immediately. Check CDFW and NMFS closure maps before deep-water rockfish fishing south of Point Conception.

yellowtail_rockfish.bag_limit: 10 per day (shelf rockfish aggregate in most areas)
yellowtail_rockfish.season: Check current CDFW/ODFW/WDFW season calendar — seasons and depths vary by area
yellowtail_rockfish.notes: Yellowtail rockfish count toward the general shelf rockfish daily bag limit. Verify current state rules and area-specific depth restrictions.

greenspotted_rockfish.notes: Counted in the general rockfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

sharpchin_rockfish.notes: Counted in the general rockfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

redbanded_rockfish.notes: Counted in the general rockfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

coho_salmon_pacific.season: Check ODFW ocean and river seasons carefully
coho_salmon_pacific.notes: Coho regulations vary by management area. Some populations are ESA-listed. Always verify current ODFW rules.

chum_salmon.season: Check ODFW for open rivers and dates
chum_salmon.notes: Chum salmon regulations vary by river. Not all rivers are open.

pink_salmon.bag_limit: No limit in ocean; river limits vary
pink_salmon.season: Ocean: July-September odd years; rivers: check ODFW
pink_salmon.notes: Pink salmon run in large numbers in odd years only. Verify current ODFW rules.

dolly_varden.season: Open in most streams year-round; check for seasonal closures
dolly_varden.notes: Dolly Varden regulations vary by river in WA and OR. Some rivers are open only for hatchery fish (adipose fin clipped). Always verify current state rules.

wahoo_pacific.notes: Billfish and large pelagics are rarely encountered in OR/WA. Verify federal NOAA HMS rules.

mahi_mahi_pacific.notes: Billfish and large pelagics are rarely encountered in OR/WA. Verify federal NOAA HMS rules.

striped_marlin.notes: Billfish and large pelagics are rarely encountered in OR/WA. Verify federal NOAA HMS rules.

pacific_sailfish.notes: Billfish and large pelagics are rarely encountered in OR/WA. Verify federal NOAA HMS rules.

pacific_grenadier.notes: No specific recreational regulations. Verify current state rules.

walleye_pollock.notes: No specific recreational regulations. Verify current state rules.

spiny_dogfish_pacific.notes: Pacific spiny dogfish have no bag or size limit. Handle with care — they have a venomous dorsal spine.

pacific_angel_shark.notes: Pacific angel sharks are fully protected in California. Release immediately if caught. Federal listing as Endangered Species applies.

bat_ray_pacific.notes: Bat ray bag limit is 2 per day in California. They have a venomous tail spine — handle carefully.

banded_guitarfish.notes: No specific regulations for banded guitarfish. Verify current state rules.

sablefish_pacific.notes: Sablefish recreational bag limit is 10 per day. Verify current ODFW/WDFW rules.

california_corbina.notes: No size limit for California corbina. 10-fish bag limit. Verify current CDFW rules.

pacific_bluefin_tuna_juvenile.notes: Check current PFMC and state rules for Pacific bluefin tuna.

pink_salmon_pacific.season: July through September odd years (WA); check ODFW for OR
pink_salmon_pacific.notes: Pink salmon runs are on odd years for most WA waters. Check current WDFW/ODFW rules.

sockeye_salmon_pacific.season: Extremely variable — check current state rules for specific water body
sockeye_salmon_pacific.notes: Sockeye salmon regulations are highly specific by location and year. Many waters have very limited or no sockeye retention. Verify current WDFW/ODFW rules.

chum_salmon_pacific.notes: Chum salmon seasons vary by water body. Check current WDFW/ODFW rules.

steelhead_tidal.min_size: Hatchery fish only in many rivers (marked by clipped adipose fin)
steelhead_tidal.notes: Steelhead regulations are extremely complex — wild steelhead must be released in most waters. Only hatchery fish (clipped adipose fin) may be retained in most rivers. Check current WDFW/ODFW rules for specific water bodies.

dolly_varden_tidal.season: Varies by region; summer through fall generally
dolly_varden_tidal.notes: Dolly Varden regulations vary by watershed. Check current WDFW/ODFW rules.

pacific_halibut_small.season: Complex season set annually by IPHC — check current year season before fishing
pacific_halibut_small.notes: Pacific halibut seasons are set by the International Pacific Halibut Commission (IPHC) and change annually. Regulations are complex and vary by area. Verify current IPHC and state rules each year.

wolf_eel.notes: Verify current state wolf eel rules.

pacific_hake.notes: No specific recreational regulations for Pacific hake. Commercial fishery is managed by PFMC. Verify current state rules.

c_o_sole.notes: Part of the California/Pacific flatfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

longfin_sanddab.notes: Sanddabs have a 30-fish daily limit in California. Verify current CDFW rules.

speckled_sanddab.notes: Part of the sanddab aggregate. Verify current state rules.

horn_shark.notes: No specific regulations for horn sharks in California. They have two venomous dorsal spines — handle carefully. Release recommended.

swellshark.notes: No specific regulations for swellsharks. Release immediately — they are a fascinating benthic species.

smoothhound_shark.notes: California limits smoothhound sharks to 10 per day. Verify current CDFW rules.

big_skate.notes: Part of the Pacific skate aggregate. Edible wing meat. Verify current state rules.

longnose_skate.notes: Part of the Pacific skate aggregate. Verify current state rules.

california_skate.notes: Part of the California skate aggregate. Verify current state rules.

albacore_pacific.notes: No specific bag limit for Pacific albacore. Verify current state and PFMC rules.

skipjack_pacific.notes: No specific recreational regulations. Verify current state rules.

oceanic_bonito.notes: No specific recreational regulations. Verify current state rules.

pacific_saury.notes: No specific recreational regulations. Verify current state rules.

rubberlip_perch.notes: Part of the surfperch aggregate. Verify current state rules.

black_perch.notes: Part of the surfperch aggregate. Verify current state rules.

pacific_chub.notes: No specific regulations for Pacific chub. Verify current state rules.

painted_greenling.notes: No specific regulations for painted greenling. Verify current state rules.

yellowfin_sole.notes: Part of the Pacific flatfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

flathead_sole.notes: Part of the Pacific flatfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

alaska_pollock.notes: No specific recreational limit for Alaska pollock. Most recreational pollock are caught incidentally. Verify current state rules.

olympic_peninsula_steelhead.notes: Wild steelhead must be released. Hatchery only. Check ODFW emergency regulations — rules change within season.

columbia_river_spring_chinook.notes: Mark-selective. Wild spring Chinook must be released in most sections. Buoy 10 fishery: check ODFW/WDFW boundary rules.

pacific_halibut_juvenile.notes: IPHC managed. Check ODFW season schedule annually.

coho_salmon_oregon_coast.notes: Mark-selective — wild coho must be released. Check ODFW.

steelhead_summer_run.notes: Wild steelhead must be released. Check ODFW emergency rules.

white_sturgeon_sport.notes: Barbless hooks required. Check ODFW river-specific regulations.

green_sturgeon.notes: Check ODFW — most Oregon rivers prohibit green sturgeon retention.

pacific_lamprey.min_size: Tribal harvest areas — check tribal regulations
pacific_lamprey.notes: Pacific lamprey have cultural significance to Pacific Northwest tribes. Sport harvest not common.

humboldt_squid.notes: Use large squid jigs (150-250g). Handle carefully — can bite and ink aggressively.

rockfish_black_blue.notes: Part of 10-fish rockfish aggregate. Depth restrictions and RCA closures apply. Descender devices required for released fish at depth.

rockfish_vermilion_canary.notes: Canary rockfish may have special restrictions within aggregate. Check CDFW/ODFW.

rockfish_copper_quillback.notes: Part of rockfish aggregate. Depth restrictions apply.

striped_surfperch.notes: Oregon 15-fish/day aggregate limit for surfperch; no minimum size. Verify current rules with ODFW.

spotfin_surfperch.notes: Oregon 15-fish/day aggregate limit for surfperch; no minimum size. Verify current rules with ODFW.

rubberlip_surfperch.notes: Oregon 15-fish/day aggregate limit for surfperch; no minimum size. Verify current rules with ODFW.

striped_bass.notes: May include slot restrictions. Verify current rules with RI DEM. Verify 2026 slot limits and season dates with RI DEM — ASMFC measures may have been updated.

summer_flounder.notes: Minimum size may change annually. Verify current year's rules with RI DEM. Verify 2026 regulations with RI DEM — minimum size reviewed annually.

black_sea_bass.season: Seasonal — check RI DEM for open dates
black_sea_bass.notes: Season and bag limits vary. Verify current rules with RI DEM.

bluefish.notes: Federal bag limit applies. Verify current limits.

tautog.season: Seasonal — check RI DEM for open dates
tautog.notes: Bag limit varies by season. Verify current rules with RI DEM.

scup.notes: Verify current limits with RI DEM.

false_albacore.notes: Not subject to state size or bag limits. Catch and release strongly encouraged.

atlantic_cod.season: Open year-round; federal closures may apply
atlantic_cod.notes: Verify federal groundfish area closures before offshore fishing.

weakfish.notes: Very restrictive bag limit due to population decline. Verify current RI DEM rules.

atlantic_bluefin_tuna.min_size: 73 in curved fork length (school/large school); 27 in (Highly Migratory Species)
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.bag_limit: Varies by HMS permit category; General category: 1 per vessel per trip
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.season: General category: June 1 – Nov 14 (approx); varies by NOAA in-season adjustments
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.notes: Bluefin tuna require a federal Highly Migratory Species permit. Size categories and quotas change in-season — ALWAYS verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

atlantic_mackerel.notes: No minimum size. Federal mackerel quota applies to commercial; recreational is generally open.

pollock.notes: Pollock are abundant on fall/winter cod trips in the Northeast; no specific state bag limit beyond federal groundfish rules.

spanish_mackerel.notes: Spanish mackerel arrive in summer; no closed season. Verify current state rules.

oceanic_whitetip_shark.notes: Oceanic whitetip shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

silky_shark.notes: Silky shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

common_thresher_shark.notes: Common thresher require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify NOAA HMS rules for current season and limits.

atlantic_wolffish.notes: Atlantic wolffish are a species of concern. Retention is prohibited in US federal waters. Release immediately.

cobia.notes: Cobia occasionally appear in these northern waters in summer. Verify current ASMFC coastwide rules.

little_tunny.notes: No size or bag limit for little tunny in most states. Primarily catch-and-release fishery; flesh is strong-flavored.

bay_anchovy.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

mummichog.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

striped_killifish.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

chain_pickerel.notes: Chain pickerel in tidal freshwater zones follow state freshwater regulations. Verify current tidal vs. non-tidal rules.

swordfish.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules and possession limits. Strong conservation ethic — most are released.

bigeye_tuna.season: Open year-round; Atlantic bigeye quota applies
bigeye_tuna.notes: Bigeye tuna are under ICCAT quota management. Verify current NOAA HMS possession limits. Charter captains must check current quota availability.

atlantic_menhaden.notes: No recreational bag or size limit for menhaden in most Atlantic states. Commercial harvest is managed by ASMFC. Cast-netting for live bait is widely practiced.

barndoor_skate.min_size: None (prohibited to retain in federal waters)
barndoor_skate.bag_limit: 0 in federal waters; verify state rules
barndoor_skate.notes: Barndoor skates are a species of concern and retention is prohibited in US federal waters. Release immediately.

silver_hake_whiting.notes: No federal or state recreational bag or size limit for silver hake/whiting. Commercial quota applies under NEFMC. A common winter nearshore species.

offshore_hake.notes: No specific recreational regulations for offshore hake. Verify current NEFMC rules for any updated stock-specific guidance.

atlantic_pollock.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
atlantic_pollock.notes: No recreational bag limit for pollock in most New England states. Excellent eating — check for any current NEFMC updates.

witch_flounder.notes: Witch flounder (gray sole) — excellent eating. No specific recreational size/bag limit in most states.

american_plaice.notes: American plaice (dab) — no specific recreational limit in most states.

greenland_halibut.notes: Greenland halibut (turbot) — primarily commercial species; no specific recreational regulations in US waters.

black_sea_bass_atlantic.min_size: 12.5-13 in TL (varies by state and season)
black_sea_bass_atlantic.season: Check current NOAA/state season calendar — varies annually
black_sea_bass_atlantic.notes: Black sea bass regulations are complex and change annually. Verify current state and federal rules before fishing.

tilefish_golden.notes: Golden tilefish have a 7-fish bag limit in most Mid-Atlantic and NE states under MAFMC rules. Verify current state and federal rules.

tautog_mid_atlantic.bag_limit: 3-10 per day (varies by state and season)
tautog_mid_atlantic.season: Check current state season — tautog have complex season closures in many states
tautog_mid_atlantic.notes: Tautog (blackfish) regulations are complex and vary significantly by state and season. Verify current state rules carefully before fishing.

scup_porgy.notes: Scup have a 9-inch minimum and 50-fish bag limit in most Mid-Atlantic and NE states. Verify current NOAA and state rules.

weakfish_seatrout.notes: Weakfish have a 1-fish daily bag limit in most Mid-Atlantic states due to stock decline. Verify current ASMFC and state rules.

flounder_winter.notes: Winter flounder seasons are complex and vary by state. Many NE states have closed winter flounder in some waters due to stock declines. Verify current state rules before fishing.

white_marlin.notes: White marlin are highly migratory and subject to NOAA HMS regulations. Requires federal HMS Angling Permit. Almost always released — they are an overfished stock. Report catches to the HMS recreational fishery observer program.

sailfish_atlantic.notes: Sailfish require an HMS Angling Permit. The Atlantic sailfish retention quota is very small — most anglers practice catch-and-release. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

striped_bass_small.min_size: 28 in (most states); 35 in (NJ recreational); check state rules
striped_bass_small.season: Open year-round in coastal waters; check current state seasons
striped_bass_small.notes: Striped bass regulations are complex and change frequently due to stock concerns. Most schoolie fish under the minimum are not eligible for harvest. Verify current ASMFC and state rules — regulations have changed significantly in recent years due to stock decline.

summer_flounder_fluke.season: May through October in most states; check current state season
summer_flounder_fluke.notes: Summer flounder (fluke) regulations differ significantly by state and are set annually. Minimum size and bag limits change each year — verify current ASMFC and state rules before fishing. NJ and NY have different rules.

american_eel.season: Open year-round (elver season is separate and highly regulated)
american_eel.notes: American eel recreational regulations vary by state. Glass eel (elver) fishery is separately managed and requires specific permits in states like ME and RI. Yellow/silver eels have size and bag limits. Verify current ASMFC and state rules.

striped_bass_adult.min_size: 28 in (most states); varies — check current ASMFC rules
striped_bass_adult.season: Coastal migratory: check current state season calendar
striped_bass_adult.notes: Striped bass regulations are under ASMFC management and have been tightened significantly due to stock decline. Size limits and seasons change frequently. Verify current state and ASMFC rules BEFORE every trip. Most states: 1 fish/day, 28-35 in minimum.

atlantic_sturgeon_catch_release.notes: Atlantic sturgeon are a federally protected species under the Endangered Species Act. Harvest, possession, or intentional targeting is PROHIBITED. Release immediately if caught. Report to NOAA.

white_perch.notes: White perch are abundant schooling fish in tidal rivers. Most states have no size limit and generous bag limits. Verify current state rules.

yellow_perch_tidal.notes: Yellow perch regulations vary by state and water body. Verify current state rules for tidal areas.

swordfish_atlantic.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS Angling Permit. 47-inch LJFL minimum, 1 fish per person per day. NOAA Observer Program may apply. Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

little_tunny_small.notes: No specific bag limit for little tunny (false albacore). Same as adult little tunny. Not recommended for eating by most anglers.

bonito_atlantic.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic bonito. Verify current state rules.

red_hake.notes: No specific size or bag limit for red hake (ling) in most NE states. Subject to NEFMC management. Verify current rules.

white_hake.notes: No specific recreational regulations for white hake. Verify current NEFMC and state rules.

spotted_hake.notes: No specific regulations for spotted hake. Verify current state rules.

american_plaice_small.notes: No specific recreational regulations for American plaice. Subject to NEFMC groundfish rules. Verify current rules.

sailor_grunt.notes: No specific regulations for grunts in Mid-Atlantic states.

menhaden_atlantic.notes: Not caught on hook and line. Used as bait and chum. Commercial harvest managed by ASMFC.

pollock_atlantic_surf.notes: No minimum size for recreational fishing in most NE states. Pollock managed under NEFMC.

tomcod_atlantic.notes: Hudson River tomcod: Check consumption advisories (PCB contamination in some areas).

atlantic_sturgeon_catch_and_release.notes: ESA ENDANGERED. Illegal to target, possess, or harm. Release immediately. Report to NOAA: 1-800-853-1964.

bluefish_large.notes: ASMFC 3-fish bag limit. Use wire or heavy mono leader — razor teeth.

bluefish_snapper_blues.notes: Same 3-fish bag limit. Wire or heavy mono leader required.

weakfish_sea_trout.notes: ASMFC: 1 fish per day. Critically low population. Handle gently — fragile mouths.

atlantic_mackerel_shore.notes: Very perishable — ice immediately. ASMFC managed commercially; no recreational bag limit.

longfin_squid.notes: EGI squid jigs under pier lights at night. Ink stains permanently. Excellent bait and eating.

blood_worm_tidal.notes: Blood worms are harvested commercially in Maine for sale as bait throughout the Northeast.

great_hammerhead_shark.notes: Great hammerhead sharks are a prohibited species under NOAA federal shark regulations — they may NOT be harvested or possessed. If caught, they must be released immediately with minimal harm. All anglers fishing for sharks in Atlantic/Gulf federal waters must have a valid NOAA HMS Angling permit. Verify current prohibited species list with NOAA.

red_drum.notes: Verify current limits with SC DNR.

spotted_seatrout.notes: Verify current limits with SC DNR.

southern_flounder.notes: Flounder regulations have been updated in recent years. Verify with SC DNR.

black_sea_bass.notes: Verify current season dates and limits with SC DNR.

sheepshead.notes: Verify current limits with SC DNR.

cobia.notes: Fork length minimum. Verify current rules with SC DNR.

pompano.notes: Verify current limits with SC DNR.

striped_bass.season: Open year-round (Santee-Cooper area has different rules)
striped_bass.notes: Rules vary by area. Verify with SC DNR.

king_mackerel.notes: Federal rules apply offshore. Verify with SC DNR.

tarpon.notes: Harvest of tarpon is prohibited in SC. Catch and release only.

greater_amberjack.notes: Federal restrictions apply; verify NOAA and SC DNR rules.

wahoo.notes: No SC state size or bag limit for wahoo.

gray_triggerfish.bag_limit: 20 per person per day (10 per person in Gulf federal waters)
gray_triggerfish.season: Open year-round state waters; federal Gulf waters: open year-round
gray_triggerfish.notes: Gulf federal waters bag limit is 10 per person. Verify state rules for any changes.

winter_flounder.notes: Winter flounder are uncommon south of New Jersey; verify current state rules.

red_snapper.season: Federal season (set annually by NOAA/SAFMC or GMFMC)
red_snapper.notes: Season dates and bag limits are set each year; verify with NOAA before fishing federal waters.

oceanic_whitetip_shark.notes: Oceanic whitetip shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

silky_shark.notes: Silky shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

sailfish.notes: Atlantic sailfish. Most released; verify current NOAA and state rules.

false_albacore.notes: No state size or bag limit for false albacore in most states.

florida_pompano.notes: Florida pompano season is open year-round in most states. Verify current state limits.

gag_grouper.season: Varies annually; seasonal closure often applies
gag_grouper.notes: Gag grouper are managed under strict quotas with seasonal closures. Verify NOAA HMS and state current season before targeting.

vermilion_snapper.notes: Vermilion snapper (beeliners) are abundant offshore and lightly regulated; 10-fish aggregate limit in most Gulf and SE states.

mutton_snapper.notes: Mutton snapper count toward the snapper aggregate limit. Verify current FL and Atlantic state rules.

cubera_snapper.notes: Cubera snapper are rare; they count toward the snapper aggregate limit. No specific separate regulation in most states.

atlantic_blue_marlin.notes: Atlantic blue marlin require an HMS recreational permit. 99 in LJFL minimum. Strong conservation ethic — most released. Verify NOAA HMS rules.

longbill_spearfish.notes: Spearfish are covered by NOAA HMS regulations. Verify current rules; most are released.

blackfin_tuna.notes: Blackfin tuna have no federal bag or size limit. Check state rules; generally no restriction for recreational anglers.

rock_hind_grouper.notes: Included in the grouper complex aggregate limit. Verify current NOAA and state rules.

yellowmouth_grouper.notes: Included in the grouper complex aggregate limit. Verify current NOAA and state rules.

swordfish.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules and possession limits. Strong conservation ethic — most are released.

bigeye_tuna.season: Open year-round; Atlantic bigeye quota applies
bigeye_tuna.notes: Bigeye tuna are under ICCAT quota management. Verify current NOAA HMS possession limits. Charter captains must check current quota availability.

atlantic_menhaden.notes: No recreational bag or size limit for menhaden in most Atlantic states. Commercial harvest is managed by ASMFC. Cast-netting for live bait is widely practiced.

cero_mackerel.notes: Cero mackerel rules are similar to Spanish mackerel in most states. Verify current FL FWC and NC/SC rules.

spotted_eagle_ray.notes: No specific bag limit but rays are considered a species of concern. Practice catch and release; they have venomous tail spines — handle with great care.

gizzard_shad.notes: No recreational regulations for gizzard shad in most states. Cast-netting permitted as bait collection.

striped_burrfish.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

sharpnose_puffer.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

balloonfish.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

atlantic_tripletail.notes: Tripletail regulations vary by state. Most SE/Gulf states have a 15 in size limit and 5-fish bag limit or less. Verify current state rules.

goldface_tilefish.notes: Goldface and blackline tilefish are part of the Gulf/Atlantic deepwater tilefish complex. Verify current NOAA/GULF COUNCIL regulations.

blackline_tilefish.notes: Goldface and blackline tilefish are part of the Gulf/Atlantic deepwater tilefish complex. Verify current NOAA/GULF COUNCIL regulations.

hogfish_atlantic.notes: Verify current state rules for hogfish. FL FWC regulations are more complex than neighboring states.

atlantic_spanish_mackerel.bag_limit: 15 per person per day in most states
atlantic_spanish_mackerel.notes: Spanish mackerel regulations are similar across SE/Mid-Atlantic states. FL has a 12-inch minimum. Verify current state rules.

almaco_jack.bag_limit: No specific bag limit (part of amberjack complex in some states)
almaco_jack.notes: Almaco jack are often grouped under the amberjack complex in state and federal regulations. Verify current rules with FL FWC or relevant state agency.

banded_rudderfish.notes: No specific regulations for banded rudderfish in most states. Verify current rules.

yelloweye_snapper.notes: Grouped under the snapper complex in most Gulf and SE states. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

wenchman_snapper.notes: Grouped under the snapper complex in most Gulf and SE states. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

permit_offshore.notes: Permit regulations vary by state. Verify current state rules.

nassau_grouper.notes: Nassau grouper are critically endangered and fully protected under federal and Florida law. Immediate release required. Violations carry significant federal penalties.

goliath_grouper.notes: Goliath grouper are fully protected in US waters. Do not target; release immediately if caught without removing from water. Violations carry federal penalties.

gulf_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states

cobia_adult.bag_limit: 1 per person per day (Atlantic); 2 per person (Gulf)
cobia_adult.notes: Cobia minimum and bag limits differ on Atlantic and Gulf coasts of Florida. Verify current FL FWC and state rules.

lesser_amberjack.notes: Part of the amberjack complex. Verify current state rules.

banded_rudderfish.notes: Part of the amberjack complex. Verify current state rules.

ballyhoo.notes: No specific regulations for ballyhoo. Primarily used as bait.

gray_snapper.notes: Verify current state rules for gray snapper (mangrove snapper).

hardhead_catfish.notes: No specific regulations for hardhead catfish. Considered a nuisance in most areas. Has venomous spines — handle with extreme care.

gafftopsail_catfish.notes: No specific regulations for gafftopsail catfish. Has venomous spines; handle carefully. Better eating than hardhead catfish.

atlantic_torpedo_ray.notes: Atlantic torpedo rays can deliver powerful electric shocks (up to 220 volts) — DO NOT TOUCH. Cut the leader and release at the waterline. No regulations but no reason to retain them.

spotted_eagle_ray.notes: Spotted eagle rays have a venomous tail barb — handle with extreme caution. They are a protected species in some states. Minimize handling and release quickly.

cownose_ray.notes: No specific regulations for cownose rays in most states. Some areas have encouraged harvest due to shellfish bed damage. They have a venomous tail spine — handle carefully.

atlantic_spadefish.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic spadefish. Verify current state rules.

florida_gar.notes: No specific regulations for Florida gar in most states.

alligator_gar.bag_limit: 1 per day in TX; no limit in some states
alligator_gar.season: Check current state season; TX requires a tag
alligator_gar.notes: Alligator gar regulations vary significantly by state. Texas requires a tag and has seasonal rules. Louisiana has no limit. Verify current state rules — alligator gar populations are a conservation concern in some areas.

spotted_gar.notes: No specific regulations for spotted gar in most states.

shortnose_gar.notes: No specific regulations for shortnose gar.

swordfish_atlantic.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS Angling Permit. 47-inch LJFL minimum, 1 fish per person per day. NOAA Observer Program may apply. Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

wahoo_gulf.notes: No specific bag limit for wahoo in Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

crevalle_jack_adult.notes: No specific size or bag limit for crevalle jack in most states. Verify current state rules.

horse_eye_jack.notes: No specific regulations. Note ciguatera risk in large fish. Verify current state rules.

bigeye_scad.notes: No specific regulations for bigeye scad. Primarily used as live bait.

jolthead_porgy.notes: Part of the Gulf porgy complex. Verify current GMFMC and state rules.

orangespotted_filefish.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

great_hammerhead.notes: Great hammerhead sharks are PROHIBITED in the Atlantic and Gulf under federal HMS regulations. Release immediately. Critically Endangered — minimize handling, use dehooking tools in the water.

bonnethead_shark.notes: Bonnethead sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Requires federal HMS Angling Permit from a vessel. 1-fish vessel limit. Mostly released.

inshore_shark.notes: Inshore shark fishing requires a federal HMS Angling Permit. Most small coastal sharks have a 1-fish vessel daily limit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

nurse_shark_juvenile.notes: Same regulations as adult nurse shark. Release recommended.

atlantic_sharpnose_shark_juvenile.notes: Same HMS regulations as adult sharpnose shark. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

spanish_mackerel_atlantic.notes: Spanish mackerel: 14-inch FL minimum on Atlantic coast, 12-inch Gulf. 15-fish daily bag limit in most states. Verify current ASMFC and GMFMC rules.

king_mackerel_small.notes: King mackerel have a 24-inch minimum and 3-fish bag limit in most states. Gulf regulations may differ. Verify current SAFMC, GMFMC and state rules.

florida_pompano_juvenile.min_size: 11 in (FL) — must be released if under minimum
florida_pompano_juvenile.bag_limit: 6 per day when at or above minimum size
florida_pompano_juvenile.notes: Juvenile pompano under the minimum size must be released. Same regulations as adult Florida pompano.

permit_small.min_size: 22 in fork length (same as flats permit)
permit_small.bag_limit: 2 per person per day (same as flats permit)

permit_large.notes: Same permit regulations apply at any size. Verify current FL FWC and state rules.

amberjack_lesser.notes: Gulf reef fish permit not required for lesser amberjack. Different from greater amberjack regulations.

menhaden_atlantic.notes: Not caught on hook and line. Used as bait and chum. Commercial harvest managed by ASMFC.

gulf_menhaden.notes: Used as bait. Commercial harvest managed separately.

gizzard_shad_tidal.notes: Cast net only — not caught on hook and line. Typically used as bait.

cobia_near_pier.notes: Gulf cobia regulations. 33-inch fork length minimum.

atlantic_croaker_large.notes: Not regulated in most states. Some states have size or possession limits for commercial harvest. Check state rules.

bull_shark_inshore.notes: NOAA HMS Angling Permit required to target sharks. Very heavy tackle required. Release strongly encouraged — bull sharks are apex predators with slow reproduction.

skipjack_tuna_shore.notes: Federal pelagic fish — no HMS permit needed for recreational hook-and-line. Dark flesh — best used as bait.

yellowfin_mojarra.notes: Not typically regulated — forage and bait species.

atlantic_spadefish_pier.notes: Not heavily regulated. Spadefish are excellent table fare — white, mild flesh.

sea_bream_pinfish.notes: Primarily used as live bait. Catch by cast net or tiny hook with shrimp.

mud_snapper.notes: Juvenile snapper in estuaries. Same regulations as the parent species (gray snapper, lane snapper) — check state rules.

grass_porgy.notes: Not separately regulated in most states.

sheepshead_porgy.notes: Not separately regulated — falls under general reef fish or porgy rules.

dwarf_sand_perch.notes: Too small to be targeted or regulated. Release if incidentally caught.

redfish_surf.notes: One oversized per person per day.

redfish_flats.notes: One oversized per person per day.

speckled_trout_sea_trout.notes: Slot 15-25 in. One over 25 in per day.

speckled_trout_winter.notes: Slot 15-25 in. One over 25 in per day.

tarpon_gulf_mexico.notes: FL: $50 tarpon tag required. Catch-and-release universal. Revive thoroughly before release.

goliath_grouper_encounter.notes: Illegal to harvest or possess. FL: cannot be removed from water without scientific permit.

red_snapper_gulf_large.notes: NOAA SERO annual season extremely short. State waters may differ. Barotrauma concern — use descender device.

manta_ray_encounter.notes: Cannot be targeted or harassed in US federal waters.

whale_shark_encounter.notes: Illegal to target or harm. Observe from 6 ft minimum distance. Do not ride or touch.

atlantic_halfbeak.notes: Primarily used as offshore trolling bait (ballyhoo). No regulations.

cobia_early_season.notes: Same rules as regular cobia. Atlantic and Gulf cobia share 33-inch minimum. 1 fish per day.

southern_flounder_gigging.notes: Gigging regulations same as rod-and-reel limits. TX has restricted fall gigging season at pass mouths.

swordfish_daytime_deep_drop.notes: HMS Angling Permit required. Minimum 47-inch lower jaw fork length.

white_marlin.min_size: No harvest in tournament circuits; 66 in LJFL if retaining
white_marlin.notes: HMS Angling Permit required. Severely depleted — release all white marlin.

blue_marlin_gulf.notes: HMS Angling Permit required. Catch-and-release strongly encouraged. 99-inch minimum if retaining.

largemouth_bass_tidal.notes: Freshwater license required. State freshwater bass regulations apply in tidal freshwater zones.

spot_croaker.notes: 25 fish per day bag limit; no minimum size. Verify current rules with TPWD.

snook.notes: Common snook in Texas (primarily Port Isabel/Laguna Madre area): 24-inch TL minimum, 1/day. Season closed Dec 1 – Jan 31 and Jun 1 – Aug 31. Verify 2026 dates with TPWD.

black_drum.notes: Texas black drum slot limit: 14–30 in TL, 5/day bag limit. Fish under 14 in or over 30 in are outside the slot and not eligible for harvest. Verify current slot rules with TPWD.

atlantic_croaker.notes: Atlantic croaker in Texas: no minimum size, 25/day bag limit. Verify current rules with TPWD.

great_hammerhead_shark.notes: Great hammerhead sharks are a prohibited species under NOAA federal shark regulations — they may NOT be harvested or possessed. If caught, they must be released immediately with minimal harm. All anglers fishing for sharks in Atlantic/Gulf federal waters must have a valid NOAA HMS Angling permit. Verify current prohibited species list with NOAA.

crevalle_jack.notes: Crevalle jack in Texas: no minimum size or specific state bag limit. Common inshore and nearshore. Verify with TPWD.

red_grouper.notes: Texas: 20-inch TL minimum, 3/day aggregate grouper. Verify 2026 Gulf season dates with TPWD and NOAA.

sheepshead.notes: Verify current limits with VA MRC.

king_mackerel.notes: King mackerel arrive off VA in summer; verify current VA MRC rules.

greater_amberjack.notes: Federal restrictions apply offshore; verify with NOAA and VA MRC.

atlantic_bluefin_tuna.min_size: 73 in curved fork length (school/large school); 27 in (Highly Migratory Species)
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.bag_limit: Varies by HMS permit category; General category: 1 per vessel per trip
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.season: General category: June 1 – Nov 14 (approx); varies by NOAA in-season adjustments
atlantic_bluefin_tuna.notes: Bluefin tuna require a federal Highly Migratory Species permit. Size categories and quotas change in-season — ALWAYS verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

atlantic_mackerel.notes: No minimum size. Federal mackerel quota applies to commercial; recreational is generally open.

oceanic_whitetip_shark.notes: Oceanic whitetip shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

silky_shark.notes: Silky shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

common_thresher_shark.notes: Common thresher require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify NOAA HMS rules for current season and limits.

false_albacore.notes: No state size or bag limit for false albacore in most states.

atlantic_bonito.notes: No state regulations for Atlantic bonito in most states.

atlantic_blue_marlin.notes: Atlantic blue marlin require an HMS recreational permit. 99 in LJFL minimum. Strong conservation ethic — most released. Verify NOAA HMS rules.

little_tunny.notes: No size or bag limit for little tunny in most states. Primarily catch-and-release fishery; flesh is strong-flavored.

bay_anchovy.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

mummichog.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

striped_killifish.notes: No state regulations for this baitfish species; may require a general bait license in some states.

chain_pickerel.notes: Chain pickerel in tidal freshwater zones follow state freshwater regulations. Verify current tidal vs. non-tidal rules.

swordfish.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules and possession limits. Strong conservation ethic — most are released.

bigeye_tuna.season: Open year-round; Atlantic bigeye quota applies
bigeye_tuna.notes: Bigeye tuna are under ICCAT quota management. Verify current NOAA HMS possession limits. Charter captains must check current quota availability.

atlantic_menhaden.notes: No recreational bag or size limit for menhaden in most Atlantic states. Commercial harvest is managed by ASMFC. Cast-netting for live bait is widely practiced.

spotted_eagle_ray.notes: No specific bag limit but rays are considered a species of concern. Practice catch and release; they have venomous tail spines — handle with great care.

cownose_ray.notes: No state regulations for cownose ray in most Mid-Atlantic states. Some states run bow-fishing and bowfishing tournaments during spring/fall runs.

gizzard_shad.notes: No recreational regulations for gizzard shad in most states. Cast-netting permitted as bait collection.

silver_hake_whiting.notes: No federal or state recreational bag or size limit for silver hake/whiting. Commercial quota applies under NEFMC. A common winter nearshore species.

atlantic_spanish_mackerel.bag_limit: 15 per person per day in most states
atlantic_spanish_mackerel.notes: Spanish mackerel regulations are similar across SE/Mid-Atlantic states. FL has a 12-inch minimum. Verify current state rules.

florida_pompano.notes: Verify current state pompano regulations as rules vary.

gulf_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
gulf_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

northern_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

wahoo_atlantic.bag_limit: 2 per person per day in most states
wahoo_atlantic.notes: Wahoo regulations vary by state. Most SE/Gulf states have a 2-fish bag limit. Verify current state rules.

black_sea_bass_atlantic.min_size: 12.5-13 in TL (varies by state and season)
black_sea_bass_atlantic.season: Check current NOAA/state season calendar — varies annually
black_sea_bass_atlantic.notes: Black sea bass regulations are complex and change annually. Verify current state and federal rules before fishing.

spot_atlantic.notes: No size or bag limit for Atlantic spot in most states. A beloved fall panfish throughout the Mid-Atlantic.

tilefish_golden.notes: Golden tilefish have a 7-fish bag limit in most Mid-Atlantic and NE states under MAFMC rules. Verify current state and federal rules.

atlantic_blacktip_shark.notes: Shark regulations require a federal HMS Angling Permit for non-Atlantic coastal state recreational fishing. Verify current NOAA HMS rules for blacktip shark.

spinner_shark.notes: Spinner sharks are managed under NOAA HMS shark rules. Verify current regulations.

caribbean_reef_shark.notes: Managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current federal shark regulations. Practice catch-and-release.

lemon_shark.notes: Lemon sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current regulations.

sand_tiger_shark.season: Check current state and federal rules
sand_tiger_shark.notes: Sand tiger sharks are protected in some states (NC, VA). Release immediately. Check current NOAA HMS and state rules.

blue_catfish_tidal.min_size: None (VA and MD encourage harvest — no minimum)
blue_catfish_tidal.notes: Blue catfish are an invasive species in Chesapeake Bay tributaries. VA and MD encourage unlimited harvest. No bag or size limit — take as many as you want.

channel_catfish_tidal.notes: No specific regulations for tidal channel catfish.

skipjack_tuna_atlantic.notes: No specific recreational bag limit for skipjack tuna in most Atlantic states. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

cobia_juvenile.min_size: Same as adult cobia — 33 in (Atlantic) or 36 in (Gulf) FL
cobia_juvenile.bag_limit: 1 per person per day (Atlantic); 2 per person Gulf
cobia_juvenile.notes: Cobia regulations apply regardless of size. Atlantic: 33 in minimum, 1 fish per day. Gulf: 36 in minimum, 2 fish per day. Verify current state rules.

redfish_juvenile.bag_limit: 1 per person per day in most states; FL Gulf 2 per day
redfish_juvenile.notes: Redfish (red drum) slot limits apply — fish outside the slot must be released. Florida Gulf: 18-27 in slot, 2 fish/day. Verify current state slot limits carefully.

tarpon_juvenile.min_size: No minimum for catch-and-release; harvesting requires special permit in FL
tarpon_juvenile.bag_limit: Catch-and-release only (FL requires tarpon tag to harvest)
tarpon_juvenile.notes: Tarpon are primarily catch-and-release. Florida requires a $50 tarpon tag to harvest a tarpon. Most anglers release all tarpon.

northern_puffer.notes: No specific regulations for northern puffer. Properly cleaning pufferfish is important — the liver, skin, and gonads contain tetrodotoxin. Only eat the skinned back-strap meat.

tautog_mid_atlantic.season: Spring and fall seasons; summer closure in most states
tautog_mid_atlantic.notes: Tautog have a summer closure in most Mid-Atlantic states. Verify current state rules.

scup_porgy.notes: Scup have a 9-inch minimum and 50-fish bag limit in most Mid-Atlantic and NE states. Verify current NOAA and state rules.

weakfish_seatrout.notes: Weakfish have a 1-fish daily bag limit in most Mid-Atlantic states due to stock decline. Verify current ASMFC and state rules.

white_marlin.notes: White marlin are highly migratory and subject to NOAA HMS regulations. Requires federal HMS Angling Permit. Almost always released — they are an overfished stock. Report catches to the HMS recreational fishery observer program.

sailfish_atlantic.notes: Sailfish require an HMS Angling Permit. The Atlantic sailfish retention quota is very small — most anglers practice catch-and-release. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

longfin_albacore.notes: No specific recreational bag limit for longfin albacore. Verify current NOAA HMS and state rules.

dolphinfish_mahi_school.notes: No specific bag limit for mahi-mahi in most states. Verify current state rules.

striped_bass_small.notes: Striped bass regulations are complex and change frequently due to stock concerns. Most schoolie fish under the minimum are not eligible for harvest. Verify current ASMFC and state rules — regulations have changed significantly in recent years due to stock decline.

summer_flounder_fluke.season: May through October in most states; check current state season
summer_flounder_fluke.notes: Summer flounder (fluke) regulations differ significantly by state and are set annually. Minimum size and bag limits change each year — verify current ASMFC and state rules before fishing. NJ and NY have different rules.

cobia_adult.min_size: 37 in FL (fork length) — 36 in most Mid-Atlantic states
cobia_adult.notes: Cobia have a 1-fish daily bag limit in most states. Atlantic coast minimum is typically 36-37 in fork length. Verify current ASMFC and state rules.

american_eel.season: Open year-round (elver season is separate and highly regulated)
american_eel.notes: American eel recreational regulations vary by state. Glass eel (elver) fishery is separately managed and requires specific permits in states like ME and RI. Yellow/silver eels have size and bag limits. Verify current ASMFC and state rules.

atlantic_torpedo_ray.notes: Atlantic torpedo rays can deliver powerful electric shocks (up to 220 volts) — DO NOT TOUCH. Cut the leader and release at the waterline. No regulations but no reason to retain them.

striped_bass_adult.season: Coastal migratory: check current state season calendar

hybrid_striped_bass.season: Open year-round in most freshwater/tidal areas
hybrid_striped_bass.notes: Hybrid striped bass are a stocked species in many reservoirs. Regulations vary by water body. Verify current state rules.

atlantic_sturgeon_catch_release.notes: Atlantic sturgeon are a federally protected species under the Endangered Species Act. Harvest, possession, or intentional targeting is PROHIBITED. Release immediately if caught. Report to NOAA.

white_perch.notes: White perch are abundant schooling fish in tidal rivers. Most states have no size limit and generous bag limits. Verify current state rules.

yellow_perch_tidal.notes: Yellow perch regulations vary by state and water body. Verify current state rules for tidal areas.

tilefish_blueline.notes: Part of the tilefish complex. Verify current SAFMC/MAFMC and state rules.

atlantic_sharpnose_shark_juvenile.notes: Same HMS regulations as adult sharpnose shark. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

spanish_mackerel_atlantic.notes: Spanish mackerel: 14-inch FL minimum on Atlantic coast, 12-inch Gulf. 15-fish daily bag limit in most states. Verify current ASMFC and GMFMC rules.

king_mackerel_small.notes: King mackerel have a 24-inch minimum and 3-fish bag limit in most states. Gulf regulations may differ. Verify current SAFMC, GMFMC and state rules.

pacific_halibut_large.notes: Brain-spike large halibut before landing. IPHC annual catch limits.

pacific_halibut.season: Seasonal — IPHC sets annual season dates
pacific_halibut.notes: Alaska Pacific halibut: 32-inch minimum, 2 fish/day. Season dates and area-specific limits set annually by the International Pacific Halibut Commission (IPHC). Verify 2026 season, area, and limits with AK F&G and the IPHC before fishing — regulations are complex.

chinook_salmon.min_size: 20 in FL minimum in most areas
chinook_salmon.bag_limit: 1 per day (most areas); 0 in some closed systems
chinook_salmon.season: Seasonal — varies significantly by area; check AK F&G Sport Fishing Regulations
chinook_salmon.notes: Alaska king (chinook) salmon regulations are among the most complex in the world. Limits, minimum sizes, and seasons vary dramatically by drainage, area, and even specific sections of river. Some systems are closed entirely to king salmon fishing to protect wild stocks. Always check AK F&G current emergency order closures and area-specific rules before targeting king salmon. 20-in FL general minimum in saltwater; many freshwater systems differ.

coho_salmon.season: Seasonal — August through November in most areas; check AK F&G
coho_salmon.notes: Alaska coho (silver) salmon: generally 6/day in most saltwater and freshwater areas. Season typically August–November. Some systems restrict to hatchery-marked fish only. Check AK F&G for area-specific rules and emergency orders — regulations change annually.

pink_salmon.season: Seasonal — odd/even year runs peak July–August; check AK F&G
pink_salmon.notes: Alaska pink (humpy) salmon are abundant in odd-numbered years in many drainages. Generally 6/day in most areas. Runs peak July–August. Check AK F&G for current-year area-specific limits, which can be very generous in high-abundance years.

sockeye_salmon.season: Seasonal — June through August in most systems; check AK F&G
sockeye_salmon.notes: Alaska sockeye (red) salmon: typically 6/day in most areas. Popular in Bristol Bay, Kenai River, and Southeast Alaska. Season generally June–August. Daily limits may be higher in some areas during peak runs. Check AK F&G for current emergency orders and area-specific rules.

dungeness_crab.season: Seasonal — varies by area; check AK F&G
dungeness_crab.notes: Alaska Dungeness crab: 6.5-inch carapace minimum, 6 male crab/day. Female crabs must be returned. Season varies by area and management zone. Check AK F&G for current area-specific rules.

lingcod.notes: Alaska lingcod: 35-inch TL minimum (stricter than most lower-48 states), 2/day bag limit. Found in shallow rocky reefs and kelp in Southeast and Southcentral Alaska. Check AK F&G for any area-specific closures.

black_rockfish.notes: Alaska nearshore rockfish (including black rockfish): 5-fish aggregate daily limit. Found around kelp beds, rocky reefs, and piers. Some deep-water species (yelloweye, canary) have much lower limits. Verify area-specific rules with AK F&G.
